selected_topics.lesson_subject: DHCP smart relay on interfaces with a secondary IP
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Per-client unanswered-request counter switches relay source identity from the primary interface address to configured secondary-interface relay addresses, then cycles back.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client DHCPDISCOVER/DHCPREQUEST -> relay using primary IP -> three unanswered requests -> relay using secondary IP -> three unanswered requests -> restart primary phase.
selected_topics.failure_class: DHCP server scope or relay-source mismatch; missing route to relay; secondary relay address not configured; no response across both source identities.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: dhcprelay debug shows transaction ID, request reception, Option 82 insertion, route lookup, forwarding source/target, DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK; the source address change proves fallback was entered.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Confirm interface primary/secondary addresses, primary and secip relay targets, route reachability, DHCP scopes for the relay identities, and Option 82 policy; use packet capture plus dhcprelay debug.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: three-unanswered-request threshold; relay source identity; DHCP debug evidence; primary-secondary-primary cycle.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: single FortiGate interface with primary/secondary addresses, one or two relay targets, and a client-to-server request/offer return path.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: ADOM-level metadata variables and mapping precedence
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Per-ADOM variable namespace with default, device-group, per-device and Global Database ADOM mapping scopes; per-device values override group values.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Define variable -> choose default and eligible mapping scope -> map device/group -> reference $variable in a supported object/template field -> render/install device-specific value.
selected_topics.failure_class: Variable resolves to default or blank; unsupported field; wrong ADOM scope; stale or missing device/group mapping; API deletion blocked by references.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Metadata Variables list and Device Manager mapping view show configured values; rendered configuration/install preview proves the value actually resolved for a target device.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Check ADOM, supported-field indicator, default, group membership, per-device override and rendered install preview; export/import mappings for controlled migration.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: mapping precedence; Global Database ADOM limitation; $variable substitution; API CRUD and reference-in-use deletion.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: ADOM variable definition branching to default/group/device mappings, then converging into a rendered template/object for a managed device.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Scheduled log aggregation between FortiAnalyzer units
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Daily scheduled FAZ-to-FAZ delta transfer over rsync/SSH; client retains received logs and sends only records not already on the receiving analyzer.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client collects device logs -> scheduled aggregation time -> authenticate to receiving FAZ as Super_User -> transfer unseen log data -> receiving FAZ indexes/displays it.
selected_topics.failure_class: Receiver not accepting aggregation; wrong Super_User credentials; unsupported syslog/CEF destination; schedule or route failure; expecting real-time forwarding semantics.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: get system log-forward shows IDs; execute log-aggregation <id> triggers a test; destination Log View shows transferred records; these do not prove real-time freshness.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Enable accept-aggregation and disk quota on receiver, verify client credentials/server IP/time, trigger one aggregation manually and compare destination records.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: forwarding versus aggregation; server accept flag; daily schedule and dedup; manual execute command.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FAZ client ingesting multiple devices, scheduled batch/delta transfer to FAZ receiver, with separate receiver acceptance/authentication gate.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: IPv6 Router Advertisement Guard: policy criteria and port/VLAN binding
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Ingress ICMPv6 Router Advertisements are evaluated against device role, M/O flags, hop-limit range, router preference, source ACL and advertised-prefix list before forwarding.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Define IPv6 source ACL/prefix list -> build RA-guard policy -> bind policy to interface and VLAN -> inspect permitted/dropped RA traffic.
selected_topics.failure_class: Unauthorized host emits RA; legitimate router RA mismatches policy; policy exists but is not bound to the active port/VLAN; wrong ACL/prefix list causes silent drops.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: get switch raguard-policy and interface configuration prove policy objects/bindings; packet capture of ICMPv6 type 134 proves actual RA ingress/egress behavior.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Classify trusted router-facing ports, allow only intended link-local sources and prefixes, bind correct policy per VLAN, then test legitimate and rogue RA frames.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: host versus router role; M/O and hop-limit criteria; ACL versus prefix-list; policy binding versus object creation.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: IPv6 access VLAN with rogue host and authorized router; RA guard on switch ingress evaluates source, flags, hop limit, preference and prefix before forwarding.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: 802.11k and 802.11v assisted roaming: neighbor knowledge, steering and capacity trade-offs
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: 802.11k supplies neighboring-AP information to clients; Fortinet's 802.11v assisted-roaming control encourages movement from congested APs; these settings interact with radio background scanning and SSID capacity.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: SSID advertises roaming capabilities -> client receives neighbor/site information -> client evaluates candidate APs -> AP/controller may encourage transition from congested coverage -> client reassociates.
selected_topics.failure_class: Client does not roam despite feature enabled; AP profile triggers background scanning and reduces available VAP count; unsupported client or mismatched SSID security prevents expected behavior.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: SSID configuration proves advertised capability; over-the-air action-frame capture and client roam logs prove negotiation and reassociation; AP profile shows scan/VAP constraints.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate client support, SSID-level 802.11k/v/11r settings, radio profile and background-scan mode; test with representative clients and measure roam interruption.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: neighbor report versus transition assistance; client decision boundary; 802.11r distinction; seven/eight VAP background-scan constraint.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: three overlapping AP cells with neighbor-report information, a congested AP steering prompt and a roaming client reassociating to a less-loaded AP.

selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: After successful 802.1X RADIUS authentication, FortiNAC uses the SSID value in RADIUS Attribute 30 to register the host to the authenticated user before network-policy evaluation.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Wireless station associates -> AP/controller sends RADIUS Access-Request with Called-Station-ID/SSID -> RADIUS accepts -> FortiNAC links host to user -> network access policy selects VLAN/role.
selected_topics.failure_class: Attribute 30 absent or does not contain the SSID; auto-registration disabled on that SSID; RADIUS success occurs but host-user association is not created.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: RADIUS request attributes prove the SSID context; FortiNAC host record and associated user prove registration; Access-Accept alone proves authentication only.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Enable Dot1x Auto Registration on the correct SSID, verify Attribute 30 format and SSID value from the controller/AP, then inspect host-user association before policy enforcement.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Attribute 30 requirement; registration-before-policy order; Access-Accept versus host registration; SSID-level scope.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wireless client through AP/controller to FortiNAC RADIUS, with Attribute 30 carrying SSID and host-user registration feeding policy/VLAN selection.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: N+1 CA failover: secondary-originated health checks and promotion control
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: One standby secondary CA can protect multiple primary CAs; the secondary performs direct and indirect health checks and promotes only when both paths fail.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC-M defines N+1 group -> secondary remains Standby -> direct check to primary -> indirect check via another primary if needed -> promotion -> manual Resume Control after primary recovery.
selected_topics.failure_class: False promotion from one failed path; mismatched firmware prevents primary membership; independent IP/backup IP misconfiguration; recovered primary remains Standby until manual control resume.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: CA Management states Standby/Promotion In Progress/Promoted; FailoverConsole getFailoverGroup shows group membership; health-check path results prove decision inputs.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Match firmware, verify primary/secondary role and backup IP, validate direct and indirect reachability from the secondary, tune supported ICMP/TCP health-check intervals and manually resume control after recovery.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: direct plus indirect check; secondary performs checks not Manager; 7.6.3 ICMP/TCP check refinement; manual Resume Control.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC-M managing two primary CAs and one standby secondary; direct and indirect health-check paths; secondary promotion and manual primary resumption.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: SAML IdP per-service-provider authorization using LDAP group filters
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator evaluates each SAML service provider's remote LDAP group filter and suppresses IdP-initiated portal entries for users who are not authorized for that SP.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User authenticates to IdP -> user/group source resolves -> SP-specific LDAP filter evaluates -> authorized SPs appear in portal -> selected SP receives assertion -> SP validates assertion.
selected_topics.failure_class: User authenticates but sees no SP; group subtype or DN/filter is wrong; user retrieval returns no member; operator confuses SAML authentication with per-SP authorization.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: SP group-filter configuration and IdP portal visibility prove policy evaluation; authorization-denial system/GUI logs prove the filter denied access.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate remote LDAP group subtype, DN/list/filter, user retrieval attribute, SP group filter and authorization-failure logs; test with users both inside and outside the group.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: LDAP directory group versus list versus advanced LDAP filter; portal hiding; authentication versus SP authorization.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Browser to FortiAuthenticator IdP, LDAP group lookup, per-SP authorization gate, then assertion to only an authorized service provider.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Secret approval profiles, tiered review, time-bounded launch and revocation
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A secret/job request is gated by an approval profile with up to three tiers; tier thresholds, approvers, request window and launch behavior determine when the secret can be used.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Secret enables approval -> requester submits Launcher or Job request -> tiered approvers review -> approval grants a bounded access window -> launch occurs only if configured/started -> revocation can terminate an active session.
selected_topics.failure_class: Approval profile not attached; request option absent; wrong request type; approved request not launched because Start Upon Approval is disabled; remote group email suppressed by Trust Time.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: My Request List and Approval List show request/status; Launcher Status timer shows remaining access; approval audit comments and session termination prove revocation behavior.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Verify secret-level approval requirement, selected profile, tier quorum, approver membership, time window, Start Upon Approval and remote-group Trust Time; test revocation with a nonproduction secret.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: three approval tiers; launcher versus job request; Start Upon Approval default; revoke-after-launch terminates session.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Requester -> FortiPAM request queue -> three-tier approval gate -> time-bounded secret launcher/job -> active session with revocation kill path.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Event aggregation, Group By attributes and threshold-based incident rules
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Rule subpatterns filter normalized event attributes, group matching events by selected keys, apply aggregate functions/thresholds and populate incident attributes.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Events normalized -> subpattern filters -> Group By partitions events -> aggregate expression threshold evaluates -> incident attributes populated -> incident created/cleared.
selected_topics.failure_class: Wrong event attributes or parser; grouping key too broad/narrow; threshold never met; scheduled-rule engine limitation; incident attributes not mapped.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Historical search proves matching events exist; rule test/incident proves rule fired; incident attributes show which group values were carried forward.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate normalized fields, choose correct Group By keys, test aggregate expression with historical data, check ClickHouse/non-ClickHouse subpattern limits, and define incident attributes.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: group-by partitioning; COUNT versus COUNT DISTINCT; scheduled rule subpattern limit; incident attribute mapping.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: normalized event stream split by filter, grouped by source/destination attributes, aggregate threshold gate, incident output and clear-condition loop.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Digital Experience Monitoring: PoP-to-SaaS health and endpoint-to-PoP TCP latency
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: DEM separates first-mile PoP-to-SaaS application health checks from managed-endpoint underlay TCP latency to the FortiSASE PoP.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: PoP health checks SaaS endpoint -> time-series metrics/drilldown; DEM agent reports endpoint-to-PoP TCP latency when endpoint is managed/online and steering bypass preserves underlay path.
selected_topics.failure_class: SaaS application absent from catalogue; endpoint agent offline/unmanaged; tunnel captures the measurement path; subscription/trial gate; chart not yet populated.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: DEM dashboard history proves PoP-to-SaaS measurement; endpoint detail Network Metrics proves endpoint-to-PoP TCP latency; neither alone proves SaaS application-layer transaction success.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Check release channel/application catalogue, subscription/trial, endpoint invitation/agent status, FQDN bypass to Turbo URL, and allow up to one day for data population.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: first-mile versus endpoint underlay; managed/online agent prerequisite; Turbo URL steering bypass; 24-hour population delay and beta caveat.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: remote endpoint with DEM agent -> underlay TCP path -> FortiSASE PoP -> SaaS app; separate metric lanes for endpoint-to-PoP and PoP-to-SaaS.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: BGP community-to-route-tag translation for dynamic SD-WAN destinations
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Inbound BGP community is matched by a route map and translated into a local route tag; an SD-WAN route-tag address object/rule matches the dynamic BGP prefixes.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Neighbor advertises prefix+community -> inbound community-list/route-map assigns route-tag -> route-tag address object matches learned prefix -> SD-WAN service selects eligible members.
selected_topics.failure_class: Route map applied outbound instead of inbound; community mismatch; route tag not assigned; route-tag object missing; SD-WAN rule order or destination match incorrect.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: get router info bgp network shows community and RouteTag; diagnose sys sdwan service shows selected members; diagnose firewall proute list shows the matched service.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Verify received community, attach route-map-in to the correct neighbor, confirm route tag, create the route-tag address object and inspect SD-WAN service/proute output.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: BGP community versus local route tag; route-map-in direction; 7.4+ route-tag address object; BGP table versus SD-WAN service evidence.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: BGP neighbor advertises changing prefixes with community; inbound route-map assigns local tag; route-tag address object feeds SD-WAN service and member selection.
